summary.text: Gary Palmer is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2014. Before Congress he spent 24 years as president of the Alabama Policy Institute, a conservative think tank that grew out of the Alabama Family Alliance he started. In the House he has chaired the Republican Policy Committee and now chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee of the Energy and Commerce Committee; he is seeking re-election after winning the August 11, 2026 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Palmer was born in Haleyville, Alabama, in 1954, and, according to his congressional website, grew up in the small town of Hackleburg in Northwest Alabama. He earned a bachelor's degree in operations management from the University of Alabama in 1977, where his website says he was a walk-on member of the football team under Coach Paul 'Bear' Bryant.

After graduating, he worked for two major international engineering and construction companies before his involvement with Focus on the Family led him to start the Alabama Family Alliance in 1989, which became the Alabama Policy Institute. He served as its president for 24 years, stepping down in 2014 to run for Congress, and also served on Gov. Robert Bentley's Alabama Commission on Improving State Government.
Wikipedia adds that Palmer helped found the State Policy Network, an umbrella organization of state-level think tanks, and served as its president.

Palmer ran in 2014 for Alabama's 6th District seat, which 11-term Republican Rep. Spencer Bachus had held and was leaving after announcing his retirement. He finished second in a seven-candidate Republican primary on June 3, won the July 15 runoff over Paul DeMarco, 64% to 36%, and won the general election over Democrat Mark Lester with 76.2% of the vote.

He took office in the 114th Congress in January 2015 and has been re-elected since. House Republicans elected him chairman of the Republican Policy Committee for the 116th Congress, defeating David Schweikert, 130-63, and re-elected him unopposed for the 118th Congress; he chaired the committee from 2019 to 2025. He is listed as a member of the House Freedom Caucus.

For 2025-2026 his committee assignments are Energy and Commerce, where he chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee, and Oversight and Government Reform. He won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 85.7% of the vote over Case Dixon, after the original May primary results were voided.
